title: Verify the Tradable Contract
objective: Apply verify the tradable contract with a source-stamped specification record.
why: Instrument identity and current specifications are prerequisites for valid risk and execution decisions.
core: An index value, ETF, CFD and futures contract are different instruments. Record venue, product, contract month, currency and data source before calculating risk.
Every example is original and synthetic. Verify live specifications, schedules and broker rules before any real decision.
This curriculum is educational and does not recommend a product, provider or trade.
scenario: A note says only "S&P at 6200" with no venue, symbol, expiry or feed.
exercise: Rewrite the note as a verification checklist and leave every unsupported field unknown.
quiz: Explain the result and its limitations.
The note is not execution-ready. A complete identity might name CME ES plus a specific month, but the case supplies no basis to invent one.
What must be rechecked before use?
The current exchange specification, schedule, data entitlement and any broker-specific operational rule.
mistake: Using a familiar ticker or chart label as proof of contract identity and current specifications.
evidence: Official CME product, schedule and market-data pages, checked 2026-10-30; original educational scenarios.

scenario: A synthetic ES move is 8.00 index points and a synthetic NQ move is 25.00 points, one contract each.
exercise: Using the cited specifications, compute gross changes before fees and explain why equal point moves are not equal risk.
quiz: Explain the result and its limitations.
ES uses $50 per index point, so 8 points is $400. NQ uses $20 per index point, so 25 points is $500.

scenario: A learner proposes an ES limit at 6200.10 and a GC limit at 2750.05.
exercise: Check both prices against the cited minimum ticks and provide the nearest valid prices on either side.
quiz: Explain the result and its limitations.
ES trades in 0.25-point increments, so 6200.10 is invalid; adjacent ticks are 6200.00 and 6200.25. GC trades in $0.10 increments, so 2750.05 is invalid; adjacent ticks are 2750.00 and 2750.10.
